reason: The text fragment (Exodus 2:16-22) depicts a local, personal conflict at a well between shepherds (רֹעִים) and the daughters of the priest of Midian. The conflict is resolved when an Egyptian man (אִישׁ מִצְרִי—Moses) intervenes to help the Midianite women. There is no depiction of a national conflict between Hebrew and Egyptian peoples in this passage. Rather, the narrative presents a personal incident of hospitality and assistance, culminating in Moses' marriage to Zipporah. The statement describing a national conflict between Hebrew and Egyptian peoples does not apply to this specific text fragment.
